question.problem:
Find $f(0)$ given that $f(t)$ is a continuous vector-valued function and $u(t)$ is continuous real-valued function for which $u(0)=3$ and 

$$
{lim}_{t\to 0}[u(t)f(t)]=⟨-18,-21,6⟩\,.
$$
question.worked_solution:
Using the scalar function multiple rule for limits, and the fact that both functions are continuous, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}[u(t)f(t)] & ={lim}_{t\to 0}u(t)\cdot {lim}_{t\to 0}f(t) \\  & =u(0)f(0) \\  & =3f(0)\end{aligned}
$$

On the other hand, we are told that

$$
{lim}_{t\to 0}[u(t)f(t)]=⟨-18,-21,6⟩\,.
$$

Therefore, we obtain the following equation which we can solve for $f(0):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}[u(t)f(t)] & =⟨-18,-21,6⟩ \\ 3f(0) & =⟨-18,-21,6⟩ \\ f(0) & =\frac{1}{3}⟨-18,-21,6⟩ \\ f(0) & =⟨-6,-7,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$
